title: Optimal LLR-Weighted Independent Trace Selection
summary: A rank-increasing highest-absolute-LLR heuristic supplies independent traces, but an efficient exact maximization method and the problem’s complexity remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine the computational complexity of, or develop an efficient algorithm for, selecting $k$ linearly independent traces from candidate samples so that the sum of their absolute log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) is maximized; the existing first-come/first-selected heuristic supplies $k$ samples by repeatedly choosing the sample with the highest absolute LLR that increases the system rank, but it does not establish an exact maximization method or its complexity.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis and combinatorial optimization of reliability-weighted trace selection.
assumptions: The selected traces must be linearly independent.
parameters: k: number of traces to select
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the computational complexity or develop an efficient exact algorithm for maximizing the sum of absolute LLRs under the linear-independence constraint.

citations.label: Side-Channel Analysis of Multiplications in GF(2128) - Application to AES-GCM

progress.summary: The source presents exact maximum-sum selection as a potentially hard combinatorial optimization problem and instead uses a first-come/first-selected rank-increasing heuristic. It leaves the exact method and computational complexity unresolved.
citation_labels: Sonia Belaïd et al., Side-Channel Analysis of Multiplications in GF(2128) - Application to AES-GCM
